definition: The process by which an AI agent decomposes a high-level goal into a sequence of intermediate steps or subtasks before or while executing them.
details: Planning capabilities are central to agentic systems tackling complex, multi-step tasks, and can range from simple linear task lists to more sophisticated, revisable plans that adapt as new information is discovered.

explainer.lead: Planning is how an AI agent breaks a high-level goal into intermediate steps or subtasks before or while carrying them out. It is central to agentic systems that tackle complex, multi-step tasks.

tiers.eli5: It is the agent making a to-do list from a big goal, and updating the list as it learns new things.
tiers.practitioner: Designers range from simple linear task lists to sophisticated plans that are revised as new information is discovered. A pitfall is a plan that cannot adapt when execution reveals surprises.
tiers.paperLevel: Planning is the decomposition of a high-level goal into a sequence of intermediate steps or subtasks, performed before or during execution; plans can be linear or revisable and adaptive.

explainer.example: Told to research a market, an agent lists subtasks — search sources, summarize findings, draft a report — and revises the list when a source turns out to be unavailable.
